verdict.summary: Strategy is no longer usefully valued as an enterprise-software vendor: the common stock is a leveraged residual claim behind 843,775 BTC, $6.67 billion of debt and $15.46 billion of preferred liquidation preference at June 30. Q2 software revenue improved 6.9% to $122.4 million, led by subscription services, but that cash engine is immaterial beside an $8.33 billion GAAP operating loss caused by bitcoin fair-value accounting. The investable question is whether repeated common and preferred issuance can add BTC per diluted share faster than dividends, interest and mNAV compression consume value. Management raised $17.06 billion through ATMs year to date and held a $3.75 billion USD reserve, providing more than 2.1 years of stated preferred-dividend and interest coverage. That reduces forced-sale risk, not structural leverage. The C grade is defensible for financing access and software recurrence, but the equity remains a complex, reflexive bitcoin vehicle. With the setup still inactive, conviction requires both the stated technical activation and evidence that incremental capital remains accretive per share.

business.overview:
Strategy earns operating revenue from enterprise analytics licenses, subscriptions, support and consulting, but Q2 subscription services supplied $62.9M of the $122.4M software total and are the only visibly expanding recurring component. Software provides cash flow and a listed-company chassis, not the dominant equity value.

The AI transmission channel is software-side: Strategy One and Mosaic can monetize governed enterprise data and AI-assisted analytics for installed customers. It is not the equity's dominant valuation channel; bitcoin holdings, capital raised per diluted share and financing costs overwhelm software economics by orders of magnitude.

The model breaks if bitcoin falls faster than liquidity can absorb fixed claims, if mNAV closes and new securities cease to be accretive, or if preferred dividends and interest outgrow the USD reserve. Software growth cannot presently repair a treasury-scale capital loss, while accounting volatility does not eliminate that economic exposure.
business.moat: The defensible asset is capital-market distribution: Strategy can issue multiple common, convertible and preferred instruments at scale, then convert proceeds into BTC. That reflexive advantage persists only while securities price above the value transferred to new investors; it is not a permanent operating moat.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Strategy's capital structure is an issuance machine, not a simple common-share count. Through July 2026 it had raised $17.06B YTD through ATM programs, while debt was $6.67B and mezzanine preferred liquidation preference was $15.46B at June 30. The $21B common ATM and separate $21B STRC preferred ATM must not be conflated: common sales dilute ownership; preferred sales add senior claims and recurring dividends. The Q2 10-Q disclosed 31.328M potential Class A shares excluded as anti-dilutive across options, awards, STRK and convertible notes. Adding those to 377.626M current basic shares gives a 408.954M minimum sensitivity, not a complete current fully diluted count because award vesting and conversion conditions can change.

filings.finding: The July 30 current report furnishes Q2 Exhibit 99.1 with $122.4M software revenue, an $8.22B GAAP net loss, 843,775 BTC and the issuer's non-GAAP BTC Yield and BTC Gain measures; it is earnings disclosure, not a financing sale.

The June-quarter 10-Q supports $49.67B digital assets, $6.67B debt, $15.46B mezzanine preferred preference and $30.89B common equity; common NAV remains deeply subordinated despite the liquidity reserve.

The 2025 10-K establishes bitcoin concentration, fair-value volatility, software cash-flow limits and extensive debt and preferred risks; it is the annual control baseline, not evidence of a new issuance.

The August 24 current report updates treasury acquisition and financing activity; it supports a point-in-time holdings change but does not by itself establish that every registered ATM capacity was sold.

This June 23 prospectus supplement establishes a separate up-to-$21B STRC preferred-stock ATM; sales create senior preferred claims and dividends, not direct dilution through newly issued common shares.

This May 6 prospectus relates to exchange or resale mechanics for covered securities; registration and exchange availability must not be presented as fresh issuer cash proceeds or automatic primary issuance.
This March 23 prospectus establishes an up-to-$21B Class A common-stock ATM; actual sales raise primary capital and dilute common ownership, unlike unsold capacity remaining under the program.
This March 23 STRC prospectus supports preferred distribution capacity and its senior economic terms; it is distinct from the common ATM and must be charged through preferred carry.
This March 23 prospectus establishes an up-to-$2.1B STRK preferred program; the instrument adds liquidation preference and dividend obligations rather than increasing the common-share count directly.

The November 6 final STRE prospectus priced 7.75M shares of 10% Series A Perpetual Stream preferred at EUR80 against EUR100 stated and liquidation value, for EUR620M gross; it superseded the preliminary filing rather than creating a second offering.

The November 3 preliminary STRE prospectus contemplated 3.5M perpetual preferred shares but was superseded by accession 0001193125-25-272591, so its share count and capacity must not be added to the final EUR620M offering.

The November 4 STRK ATM supplement replaced the prior STRK program with up to $20.341B remaining capacity after 6,618,518 prior STRK shares produced $659.368M; these are 8% convertible preferred claims, not common ATM proceeds.

The November 4 STRD ATM supplement replaced the prior program and reported $4.134B remaining capacity after 774,983 prior STRD shares generated $66.2M; it is perpetual preferred financing, not debt or direct common issuance.

The November 4 STRF ATM supplement replaced the prior program and reported $1.660B remaining capacity after 3,970,812 prior STRF shares generated $440.032M; the security adds preferred liquidation and dividend claims ahead of common.

The November 4 Class A common ATM supplement replaced the prior common program and reported $15.854B remaining after 13,032,625 prior common shares generated $5.146B; only actual sales are primary dilution, while remaining capacity is not issuance.

The November 4 STRC ATM supplement established $4.2B of replacement preferred capacity and stated that no shares had been sold under the prior program; it must not be counted as completed proceeds or common-share dilution.

contrarianRisks: Separate common and STRC ATM programs create different dilution and seniority outcomes; headline capital raised is not automatically common-share accretion.
Preferred dividends of $400.7M in Q2 are real recurring claims even when BTC Yield is positive.
The USD reserve reduces near-term forced-sale risk but is finite and does not hedge BTC drawdowns.
Bitcoin fair-value accounting makes GAAP earnings volatile, but dismissing the loss entirely ignores the common equity's economic BTC exposure.
BTC Gain and BTC Yield are management-defined non-GAAP KPIs and must be tested per diluted share after financing costs.

macro.impact: MSTR is a levered BTC-duration instrument: bitcoin direction changes asset value, while equity-risk appetite determines mNAV and therefore whether new issuance is accretive. Rates also set the opportunity cost and refinancing burden of preferred and debt claims; enterprise-software demand is a distant third-order driver.

risks.riskSummary: The dominant risk is a three-way squeeze in which BTC declines, mNAV compression and fixed preferred or debt service simultaneously damage common NAV, close the financing window and force future capital to be raised on progressively less accretive terms. Retail war-room: assume a weekend BTC move or overnight offering can gap MSTR through $125.04; use regular-session liquidity and limit orders to control spread and slippage, size the position for a discontinuous loss beyond the stop, avoid entry around treasury or financing filings, and never chase more than 3% above the $135.89 activation.
